title: Decide single owner repo for the offline ROMpler demo (7db vs hcy)
description:
Decide which repo owns the canonical offline ROMpler demo. Two beads originally described the same deliverable: auxide-hcy (Create offline ROMpler demo, CLOSED in the auxide kernel store — examples/rompler_demo.rs exists) and auxide-midi-7db (Offline ROMpler demo producing .wav, now also CLOSED in the auxide-midi store; close reason: examples/rompler_demo.rs already exists, compiles (gate --all-targets clean), and runs producing rompler_demo.wav Peak 0.968 / RMS 0.504, non-silent). The duplication has therefore already been collapsed by closure — both repos ship a working rompler_demo.rs. Decide which is canonical and record it on auxide-fxw so the work is not done twice and verify_all.sh exercises exactly one demo.

## Acceptance Criteria
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. A single canonical ROMpler demo owner is chosen (kernel auxide-hcy OR auxide-midi-7db) and recorded on auxide-fxw's design as "Canonical ROMpler owner: <repo>".
2. The non-canonical demo bead is closed as a satisfied reference pointing at the canonical owner, so no duplicate build effort remains.
3. verify_all.sh exercises exactly one rompler_demo (the canonical); if the other repo keeps its example, it is clearly marked non-canonical.
4. `./verify_all.sh` (or `cargo test --workspace`) passes green after the decision is recorded.

## Definition of Done
The ROMpler duplication is resolved on paper and in the repo: one canonical demo, one reference, verify_all.sh green, decision persisted on auxide-fxw.

title: Verify full-suite end-to-end compile and test across all four crates
description:
Verify full-suite end-to-end compile and test across all four crates (auxide, auxide-dsp, auxide-io, auxide-midi), which are linked by path dependencies. Today there is no single repeatable command that proves the whole stack builds, lints, and tests together, and no cross-crate smoke test that proves a DSP graph actually renders through the kernel and is drivable by the MIDI bridge.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A single script `verify_all.sh` cd's into each of the four crates and runs `cargo build`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`; all exit 0 on a clean checkout.
2. Every crate is warning-clean under `-D warnings`.
3. NEW cross-crate smoke test: build a SynthBuilder graph (auxide-dsp) → RuntimeCore::new_with_channels (auxide) → render offline → assert non-zero; and construct MidiBridgeConfig + exercise VoiceAllocator/VoicePool on NoteOn/NoteOff (no real device needed).
4. README documents the `verify_all.sh` command as the integration gate.

## Design
A. Write `verify_all.sh` looping the four crates with build/test/clippy.
B. Add cross-crate integration test using SynthBuilder + RuntimeCore + render_offline.
C. Add a MIDI-path test building MidiBridgeConfig + allocator.
D. Wire command into README. Run; iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Write verify_all.sh AND verify_all.ps1 looping for c in auxide auxide-dsp auxide-io auxide-midi: (cd $c && cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings) || exit 1.
B. Add cross-crate integration test in auxide-midi/tests using auxide_dsp::builders::SynthBuilder + auxide::rt::RuntimeCore::new_with_channels + auxide::rt::render_offline_handle to render and assert non-zero.
C. Add MIDI-path test building MidiBridgeConfig::default() and exercising VoiceAllocator/VoicePool on NoteOn/NoteOff (no device).
D. Wire verify_all into README CI/verification section.
E. Run both scripts; iterate until all four crates green.

NOTE: dev env is win32 - verify_all.ps1 must run locally; .sh targets CI/Linux (git-bash/WSL).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A single gate (verify_all.sh for CI/Linux AND verify_all.ps1 for Windows) cd's into each of the four crates and runs cargo build, cargo test, and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; all exit 0.
2. Every crate is warning-clean under -D warnings, including tests and examples (via --all-targets).
3. NEW cross-crate smoke test in auxide-midi/tests: build a SynthBuilder graph (auxide-dsp) -> RuntimeCore::new_with_channels (auxide) -> render_offline_handle(handle, frames) (auxide) -> assert non-zero; plus MidiBridgeConfig + VoiceAllocator/VoicePool on NoteOn/NoteOff (no device).
4. README documents the verify_all command as the integration gate.

CORRECTION: use render_offline_handle (new RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCore), NOT legacy render_offline (old Runtime) - they are incompatible.
notes: TECHNICAL CONTEXT: auxide-dsp is now at v0.2.0. Check Cargo.toml dependencies in auxide-midi and auxide-io to ensure they reference compatible versions. The auxide-dsp crate has been restructured (legacy DspNode modules deleted, builders now wire edges, RT test uses counting allocator).

title: Design first-class runtime control for external DSP nodes
description:
Design first-class runtime control for external DSP nodes. The auxide kernel already provides the control plane: the ControlMsg enum and canonical `PARAM_*` indices in src/control.rs, the `NodeDef::set_param`/`gate` trait methods, and `RuntimeCore::apply_control_msg` routing in src/rt.rs. This bead formalizes and tests that contract so ANY external node (e.g., auxide-dsp) can be driven live from the main thread without breaking RT safety. It is the producer side consumed by dsp-4y9.1 and midi-u4h.1.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide -- -D warnings` clean.
2. `control.rs` documents the canonical `PARAM_*` index contract and `apply_control_msg` routes every semantic ControlMsg (SetFrequency/SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance/SetDetune/SetWaveform/SetPan/TriggerGate/AllNotesOff/Mute/Reset) onto the matching NodeDef method.
3. NEW test `apply_control_msg_routes_all`: a recording TestExternalNode (records set_param idx + gate calls) is driven by each ControlMsg variant; assert every variant reaches the expected NodeDef call.
4. NEW test `param_index_contract`: `SetParam{param_idx: PARAM_CUTOFF, ..}` reaches `node.set_param(PARAM_CUTOFF, ..)` (proves canonical indices are the single contract).

## Design
A. In control.rs add a doc comment block enumerating the canonical PARAM_* indices and meaning.
B. In rt.rs add `#[cfg(test)] apply_control_msg_routes_all` using a recording TestExternalNode; send each ControlMsg and assert.
C. Add `param_index_contract` asserting PARAM_CUTOFF passthrough.
D. Reference this contract from dsp-4y9.1 and midi-u4h.1. Iterate until green.
design:
PLAN:
A. In control.rs, add a doc comment block enumerating the canonical PARAM_* indices and their meaning (single source of truth).
B. In rt.rs add `#[cfg(test)] apply_control_msg_routes_all` using a TestExternalNode that records (param_idx, value) on set_param and on/off on gate; send each ControlMsg and assert.
C. Add `param_index_contract` asserting the PARAM_CUTOFF passthrough.
D. Reference this contract from dsp-4y9.1 (consumer) and midi-u4h.1 (producer). Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide -- -D warnings` clean.
2. `control.rs` documents the canonical `PARAM_*` index contract and `apply_control_msg` routes every semantic ControlMsg (SetFrequency/SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance/SetDetune/SetWaveform/SetPan/TriggerGate/AllNotesOff/Mute/Reset) onto the matching NodeDef method.
3. NEW test `apply_control_msg_routes_all`: a recording TestExternalNode (records set_param idx + gate calls) is driven by each ControlMsg variant; assert every variant reaches the expected NodeDef call.
4. NEW test `param_index_contract`: `SetParam{param_idx: PARAM_CUTOFF, ..}` reaches `node.set_param(PARAM_CUTOFF, ..)` (proves the canonical indices are the single contract).

title: Cross-crate forward plan: integration gate + DSP/MIDI/IO sequencing
description:
Cross-crate forward plan for the auxide stack (auxide / auxide-dsp / auxide-io / auxide-midi). Bead stores are the source of truth — one SQLite store per crate, exported to git-synced JSONL. The integration gate (auxide-b7x) is CLOSED: verify_all.sh loops all four crates with -D warnings, tests/integration_gate.rs proves SynthBuilder -> RuntimeCore::new_with_channels -> render_offline_handle -> non-zero plus the MIDI voice pool note-on/off, and the README documents the command. DSP and MIDI feature work is largely DONE (see closed beads: dd4, swx, bqj, xlw, 6yx, 85b, 9t2, etq, e9l, m13, 6jy, 43r, 28y, 1mv, gr6 in auxide-dsp; 1e4, my5, qi2, yk7, bgq, 7db, midi-u4h.1 in auxide-midi). This epic is a roadmap; child work lives in the per-crate stores and is referenced by ID below.

ACTUAL OPEN INVENTORY (per bd, 2026-07-25) — 17 open beads:
- auxide (kernel): auxide-634 (P1, ROMpler ownership decision), auxide-fxw (this epic)
- auxide-dsp: auxide-dsp-1ps (P3, PitchDetector)
- auxide-midi: auxide-midi-4kp (P2, HW-blocked MicroFreak demo — defer, must not gate release)
- auxide-io: 13 beads — m71, rfi, alz (P2); 256, 9k4, bzb, c31, gr3, ipv, lab, r4w, uk1, uzi (P3)

NOTE: an earlier version of this epic falsely claimed "32 open beads" and that 7 DSP beads "remain open". Both are incorrect; this text is the corrected source of truth.

## Success Criteria
GATED EXIT — this epic closes only when:
1. auxide-634 decision is recorded here (Canonical ROMpler owner) and verify_all.sh exercises the canonical demo.

title: auxide-conductor: orchestration layer (live server + composition)
description:
PROGRAM: turn the firmed auxide engine room into a Rust SuperCollider — a live, addressable synthesis SERVER plus a COMPOSITION crate, in one language (Rust). This is the next architectural layer above the 4 existing crates (auxide / auxide-dsp / auxide-midi / auxide-io).

ARCHITECTURE DECISION (purity check on "Conductor"):
A monolithic "Conductor" that both hosts the live graph AND composes is impure — it fuses a stateful real-time host with a stateless event generator. This is exactly the SC split: scsynth (server) vs sclang (language). Purest Rust design keeps that split in ONE language:
- SERVER (scsynth role): live, addressable node-graph host. Built INTO auxide (kernel) as a Server/GraphHost API — the server IS the engine running live; a separate crate only adds cross-crate friction on the hottest path. (Alternative if separation preferred later: auxide-server crate.)
- CONDUCTOR (sclang role, NEW crate auxide-conductor): composition — Patterns/Streams/sequences — as a Rust library, no new GC'd language.

CRATE SLICING (future): engine (auxide/dsp/midi/io, firming) -> server (in auxide) -> conductor (auxide-conductor). New crate count: 1 (auxide-conductor).

BUCKET A (DO NOW, existing stack — firm the engine room):
- Finish the 17 currently-open beads: auxide-io x13 (m71, rfi, alz, uk1, r4w, ipv, lab, bzb, 256, 9k4, gr3, c31, uzi), auxide-dsp-1ps, auxide-midi-4kp (deferred/HW-gated), auxide-634 (ROMpler ownership), auxide-fxw (tracker, closes last).
- auxide-mod: graph-native audio-rate modulation (wire output->input at audio/control rate) — prerequisite for the server; params driven by the graph, not only the control queue.
- Buffer/sample resource type in auxide-dsp (stepping stone to server buffers).
- Lock + document the RT contract (no alloc in callback; verify_all.sh + CountingAlloc as the gate) and a stable public API across the 4 crates.

BUCKET B (FUTURE — architected into the server + auxide-conductor):
- auxide-srv: live server core (node tree: groups, order-of-execution; dynamic SynthDef instantiation from a UGen registry by name; many simultaneous synth instances).
- auxide-bus: audio + control buses first-class, typed, routable.
- auxide-buf: buffers as server resources + sound-file I/O (hound), FFT-ready.
- auxide-sch: sample-accurate scheduler + transport clock (server-side).
- auxide-proto: OSC/WebSocket protocol + client (headless, addressable, live-coding-capable).
- auxide-cond (auxide-conductor crate): composition — Patterns/Streams/sequences; emits ControlEvents/GraphDefs to the server.
- (Far) embedded scripting (Rhai), parallelism (supernova-like), UGen/analysis breadth (FFT, PVoc).

WHAT WE KEEP FROM SC / LEAVE BEHIND:
KEEP: live node-tree server, groups/buses/order-of-execution, dynamic SynthDef instantiation, graph-native audio-rate modulation, buffers, sample-accurate scheduling/transport, composition (Patterns), network protocol for live-coding.
LEAVE BEHIND: the sclang<->scsynth two-language split; OSC-as-the-only-stringly-typed interface; the C++ UGen plugin API (DoneAction/custom memory) -> replaced by trait UGens in a registry; sclang's 30-year cruft/GC; supernova/scsynth divergence and build sprawl.
## Success Criteria
GATED EXIT — this epic closes only when:
1. auxide-hlf.1 (live server core) exists: auxide runs as a live, multi-instance, addressable node-graph server with graph-native modulation (auxide-pl0 done).
2. auxide-hlf.2 (buses), auxide-hlf.3 (buffers + file I/O), auxide-hlf.4 (sample-accurate scheduler + transport) are implemented in the server.
3. auxide-hlf.5 (OSC/WS protocol) + auxide-hlf.6 (auxide-conductor crate) exist: a Pattern in auxide-conductor can spawn a synth on the headless server and drive it in-time over the protocol, end-to-end.
4. RT contract preserved across engine + server (no alloc in callback; verify_all.sh + CountingAlloc green).
5. auxide-fxw (engine room, Bucket A) is closed before this epic's children begin.

## Definition of Done
auxide is a Rust SuperCollider: firmed engine room + live server + composition crate, one language, SC's good parts without the hot mess.
CRATE ARCHITECTURE (Bucket B) — decided 2026-07-25:

DO NOT split bus/buffer/scheduler into separate crates. They are mutated on the audio thread every block and are tightly coupled to node execution; separate crates would force cross-crate Arc/Mutex or trait boundaries on the hottest path (worse perf + ergonomics). Split by BOUNDARY, not concern:

THREE NEW CRATES:
1. auxide-server (NEW) — live, addressable, multi-instance synthesis server. Owns the audio thread. Modules: server::graph, server::bus, server::buffer, server::time, server::engine, server::api. Depends on: auxide (engine: NodeDef/RuntimeCore/control), auxide-dsp (nodes + register_dsp_ugens), auxide-io (StreamController backend), auxide-proto (implements protocol). Bus/buffer/time are MODULES of this crate, not crates.
2. auxide-proto (NEW) — wire boundary: OSC + WebSocket message types + Client trait. Depended on by auxide-server (implements) and auxide-conductor (uses). Boundary crate; no audio-thread code.
3. auxide-conductor (NEW) — composition: Patterns/Streams. Depends ONLY on auxide-proto (backend-agnostic). The sclang role as a Rust library.

CRATE DEPENDENCY DIRECTION:
  auxide-server  -> auxide + auxide-dsp + auxide-io + auxide-proto
  auxide-conductor -> auxide-proto
  auxide-proto   -> std + osc/ws libs only
  auxide-midi becomes a client/app (or example), NOT a server dependency.

CORE HANDLES (clear + definable):
  Server, ServerHandle (Clone+Send), SynthId, GroupId, AudioBusId, ControlBusId, BufferId,
  SynthDef (data), UGenSpec, Connection, Endpoint (NodePort|AudioBus|ControlBus),
  ScheduledEvent { target_frame, action }, Transport { bpm, beat_phase }, Client, Pattern/Stream.

INSIDE auxide-server:
  graph: Registry (name->factory fn), SynthDef (data: nodes+connections+params), NodeTree (groups + order-of-execution via topo sort; FeedbackNode for cycles), Voice (a RuntimeCore instance = one running synth).
  bus: AudioBus/ControlBus, BusArena; Endpoint can be a bus (unifies with connections).
  buffer: Buffer (Arc<Vec<f32>> + meta), BufferArena; load/save WAV via hound; Sampler/ROMpler use BufferId.
  time: Scheduler (min-heap by target frame), Transport (tempo/beat phase derived from frame).
  engine: audio callback — per block: advance frame -> drain scheduler (apply ScheduledEvents) -> apply control events (lock-free ControlMsg queue) -> execute NodeTree in order-of-execution -> write outputs to auxide-io backend. RT contract: zero alloc, lock-free.
  api: Server::new(backend), Server::handle()->ServerHandle (Clone+Send); ServerHandle::spawn_synth/set_param/connect/free/load_buffer/transport. Maps auxide-proto messages to engine ops.

MODULATION MODEL (ties to Bucket A auxide-pl0):
  Graph-native: Connection wires a node output port -> another node input port at audio OR control rate (source executed before dest in order). External: MIDI/automation arrive via lock-free ControlMsg queue, translated to set_param on the target Voice. Both coexist.

BEAD LAYERING (this epic's children):
  fxw (engine room) blocks auxide-hlf (epic).
  auxide-pl0 (graph-native modulation, Bucket A) blocks hlf.2 (graph module).
  hlf.2 (graph) blocks hlf.3 (bus), hlf.4 (buffer), server-engine, server-time.
  hlf.3, hlf.4, server-engine, server-time, hlf.5 (proto) block hlf.1 (auxide-server crate integration).
  hlf.5 (proto) + cond-core block hlf.6 (auxide-conductor crate).

title: Server crate: integration + public API (auxide-server)
description:

Owns the audio thread; hosts a live, multi-instance, addressable node graph with groups + order-of-execution; dynamic SynthDef from a UGen registry; graph-native + queue modulation; buses (audio/control), buffers + file I/O, sample-accurate scheduler + transport; exposes Server/ServerHandle (Clone+Send); implements auxide-proto server side. title: Graph-native audio-rate modulation (Bucket A)
description:
Graph-native audio-rate modulation for the auxide kernel (Bucket A, prerequisite for the live server). Today params are set via the control queue (ControlMsg -> NodeDef::set_param). Add the ability to PATCH any node output into any node input at audio OR control rate, so an LFO/SinOsc output can drive a freq input directly — SC's elegant modulation model — while the queue remains for external/MIDI events.

## Acceptance Criteria
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. A node output port can be wired to another node's input port at audio rate and at control rate.
2. A wired modulation updates every block with no per-block allocation (RT-safe).
3. Coexists with the existing ControlMsg queue (external events still work).
4. cargo test -p auxide green; clippy -D warnings clean; a test proves an LFO output audibly modulates a downstream param.

## Definition of Done
auxide supports graph-native modulation (output->input wiring), removing the main expressive gap vs SC before the server layer is built.
design: Wire node output->input at audio/control rate in auxide kernel. Prerequisite for auxide-srv. Coexists with ControlMsg queue.
acceptance_criteria: GATED EXIT: output->input wiring at audio+control rate; RT-no-alloc; coexists with queue; LFO-modulates test.
